title: Essay Film
description: In this hybrid theory/practice seminar, we analyze the category of films referred to as essay films. Described as resisting classification, interrogating boundaries between fact and fiction, and transgressing dominant ways of seeing and thinking, essay films draw from and subvert a range of established practices, including nonfiction, narrative, and avant-garde cinema. What is the history of essayistic filmmaking? What does the essayistic mode offer filmmakers and scholars today? Through readings, screenings, student-led presentations, and exercises, students will gain both a conceptual foundation and hands-on experience with the essay film. The course culminates in a final independent project.
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Flesh and Blood
description: Once considered low and marginal, the horror genre is an integral component of todays popular media culture with the formerly reviled and exiled revenant (the animated corpse) now part of the family of stock characters routinely encountered on film and TV, the internet and gaming world. This course explores the cultural and psychological implications of the current fixation on post-apocalyptic scenarios and the return of the dead.
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Fan Culture
description: This course allows students to closely examine and analyze the communities that arise around the shared enjoyment of an aspect of popular culture.
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Film Festivals
description: Examines the history of the film festival as cultural form, media network and economic practice well as related concepts of curation, taste, and prestige. Students gain experience in public programming of film series and competition programs.
prerequisites_raw: Film Studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: The Future of Media
description: This seminar takes a critical-industrial approach to analyzing 21st century digital media culture. We survey ongoing developments related to social media, streaming media, advertising, business models, and content development, among other topics, throughout the quarter. We also look at the various stakeholders ranging from Hollywood studios, Big Tech corporations, music and gaming companies, and YOU - the user - in order to understand the forces controlling, directing, creating, obstructing, and/or unleashing whatever is on the horizon for medias future.
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis Global Cinema Going
description: Explores prevailing themes in contemporary and historical film exhibition in a variety of global contexts. Readings include scholarly work and popular sources to assist students in reflecting on the research process and preparing a high-quality paper.
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Global Genres
description: Discusses the transnational iterations of diverse genrescomedy, melodrama, science fiction, action cinema, and horror to situate genres as expressive forms that respond to popular anxieties around change, movement, and dislocation engendered by the geopolitical flux.
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: Gender, Romance, and Cinema
description: Explores how films about romantic love shape, reinforce, or challenge cultural norms of gender and sexuality. Focusing on romantic comedies, melodramas, and global reworkings of these genres, the course traces how constructions and critiques of romance appear in cinema from classical Hollywood to the present. Readings from feminist film theory, queer theory, and sociology guide discussions on spectatorship, heteronormativity, gender performativity, race and masculinity, and more.
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
